run_note: Selected a comparative technical review of Langfuse vs Phoenix for agent observability. The review addresses a distinct engineer decision: choosing an observability backbone for agent workflows. Evidence covers trace hierarchy, tool/retrieval error visibility, retry handling, token/cost accounting, evaluation linkage, SDK support, export/portability, redaction, operating burden, and local/small-team deployment costs. Sources checked October 25, 2026. Artwork generation unavailable in this runtime; handoff blocked pending illustration.

candidates.title: Langfuse vs Phoenix for Agent Observability: A Comparative Technical Review
candidates.reader_outcome: Choose an observability backbone for agent workflows based on documented capabilities, architectural trade-offs, and conditional scenario recommendations.
candidates.reason: Existing guides cover agent-environment permissions and RAG evaluation but not a dedicated comparison of observability platforms for agent tracing. Langfuse and Phoenix represent the two dominant architectural approaches (ClickHouse-backed full platform vs SQLite/Postgres lightweight OTel-native). This comparison fills a reader decision gap with no duplicate in published guides or open PRs.
